home.headline: UCLA endures injury scare, gets heroic return to stay unbeaten
home.blurb: It was a heroic return for the veteran who had departed UCLA’s game against Illinois just before halftime with a sore elbow and ankle. The crowd serenaded Dieffenbach with cheers anew once he came onto the field with his team holding a suddenly precarious lead over Illinois. All Dieffenbach did upon his return was to complete each of his five passes on the next drive, including a beautiful touchdown toss, to help the fourth-ranked Bruins hold on for a 22-14 victory that kept their unbeaten record intact. “That’s leadership, that stands out,” Chesney said, “and there’s the confidence everybody gained from that.” Illinois closed to within 19-14 after quarterback Katin Houser converted a huge fourth-down play, finding wide receiver Collin Dixon in the back of the end zone for a 7-yard touchdown with 7:14 left. But the Fighting Illini could conjure no more late magic after Houser went out with his own injury. “When we walked out there, I was like, damn, yes,” Chesney said of the crowd. “I knew we were on the brink of it and you were worried about the weather, but ultimately what a great job by them and really proud of the way they showed up.” After taking a shot in the arm, Ty Dieffenbach delivered one. Roars accompanied the previously injured UCLA quarterback with each step he took as he jogged back from the locker room to the Rose Bowl sideline late in the third quarter Friday night. “That crowd reaction was unbelievable,” Dieffenbach would say later. “I mean, that was one of the best moments of my life.” “They just don’t give up, they just don’t,” UCLA coach Bob Chesney said of his players. “They just believe they have a shot to win every game and they’re going to find a way.” The Bruins could exhale only after an Illinois pass fell incomplete over the middle with 43 seconds left. UCLA had registered another big defensive play only minutes earlier when safety Scooter Jackson came up with an interception – his second of the game – and returned it 41 yards to the Illinois 19-yard line with 2 minutes 42 seconds left. A short Mateen Bhaghani field goal gave the Bruins a 22-14 lead, necessitating a desperation drive by the Fighting Illini that came up well short. There were feel-good vibes all around after Dieffenbach escaped injury and UCLA improved to 10-0 for the first time since 1998 – the last season it won a conference championship. “No one believed that UCLA would be 10-0 this year, no one in the country, no one anywhere,” linebacker Sammy Omosigho said, “and we had to make them believe.” The Bruins, who are 7-0 in Big Ten games, need only one more victory in their final two regular-season games – against Michigan and USC – to clinch an appearance in the conference title game. Among other things, a season-high crowd of 45,800 celebrated a UCLA defense that intercepted three passes and registered five tackles for loss while holding the Fighting Illini (6-4, 4-3) to 240 yards of offense. But the Hoosiers, who have yet to announce a starting quarterback for the game, can calm the waters by notching a quality win over the visiting Trojans. USC is lagging outside the CFP picture…for now. That will change if the Trojans can upset IU on the road after beating Ohio State in their last game during Week 9. A win would also catapult USC into the Big Ten title race, revitalizing a season that appeared to be in peril after a 24-7 loss at Wisconsin on Oct. 24. The question is which Indiana quarterback the Trojans will be tasked with defending. Season-long starter Josh Hoover injured his throwing arm during Indiana's Week 9 win over Minnesota and was benched after subsequent struggles. Veteran backup Grant Wilson entered and completed 9 of 17 passes for 156 yards and a touchdown, sparking a quarterback controversy. Hoosiers coach Curt Cignetti was noncommittal this week on who will take the first snaps for IU, forcing USC to be ready for either option. The situation has created some late-season intrigue for the reigning national champions, who have been unable to pull away from most of their Big Ten opponents during an 8-1 (5-1 Big Ten) start. Physical receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh comprise one of the best 1-2 tandems in college football. Meanwhile, IU running backs Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr . are both averaging more than five yards per carry and are over 700 yards each for the season. USC has never been known for its physicality under coach Lincoln Riley, but keeping the Hoosiers in check will require it. Going on the road and winning against a team with Indiana's gritty DNA wouldn't just be a huge boost for the Trojans' playoff aspirations; it would also help change the perception of Riley's program. Indiana's CFP outlook: Indiana's chances of making the playoff will reach near "lock" status at 96.2% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. A loss would leave the Hoosiers with a 66.8% chance of selection and bring greater scrutiny to a resume lacking high-end fare. An Oct. 10 win over Nebraska is not aging well, as the Cornhuskers are on a four-game losing streak. After that, IU's best win is either on the road against a 5-4 Michigan team or at home against a 6-3 Northwestern team. However you slice it, the Hoosiers don't have a win against a team currently ranked in the CFP Top 25. Beating USC would change that...assuming the Trojans remain in the rankings. USC's CFP outlook: This is do-or-die for USC's playoff hopes. The Trojans' chances of making the field will rise to 51.5% with a win and plummet to 3.7% with a loss. In other words, the playoff has already started for Lincoln Riley's team. It's really a simple formula: finish 3-0 with wins over Indiana, Maryland and USC, and the Trojans will unquestionably make the playoff for the first time. Lose any of those games, and it's probably over for what is arguably the most historic program to have never appeared in the CFP. picks.blurb: No team should be judged by how they perform when everything is going its way, just as this Ole Miss program should be judged on how it can respond after the tumult it faced last time out against Georgia. With the Rebels' playoff hopes dwindling to the lowest they have been all season, Pete Golding's squad will need to respond in a big way this afternoon in Norman . Facing an Oklahoma team with a retooled offensive scheme and rejuvenated belief in itself, Ole Miss will need to capitalize on the trend that the Sooners have yet to win consecutive games this season. Just about everything went wrong at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium last weekend for the Rebels, and it's true; everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face. Golding's side took a clean hit to the jaw from the Bulldogs, and Ole Miss will need to claw itself up against Oklahoma if it wants a chance at getting back to the playoffs this season. Trinidad Chambliss Plays a Clean Game Following His Worst Showing Numbers talk, and for Trinidad Chambliss, they're quite damning. Throwing nine passes to the wrong side this season, the Rebels' former Heisman frontrunner is third in the Football Bowl Subdivision for interceptions this year. If Ole Miss wants to win on the road tomorrow and show that it can play in tough road environments, Chambliss will need to clean the turnovers up. The differences between Georgia and Oklahoma are clear, and I truly believe that Chambliss will return to the form he got fans used to in the 2025 season. The Rebels need their star to play a professional game today, and that all starts with taking care of the ball and making the right decisions when the Sooner pass rush gets in his way. The days of Chambliss and Kewan Lacy backfields are over this year, and the former will need to remind the Rebels' faithful of the leader he is capable of being. Behind a reworked offensive line, I expect Chambliss to erase the doubts that have been growing surrounding him recently, and #6 will lead Ole Miss to victory in Norman on the heels of a strong offensive showing. Shekai Mills-Knight has the Best Rushing Performance of the Season While Lacy's legacy in Oxford looks like it will end full of questions about injuries and unfulfilled potential, the Rebels have a tailback capable of reshaping the team's rushing narrative late in the season. I wholeheartedly believe in Ole Miss' French-Canadian sophomore, and John David Baker's offensive scheming needs to rely on the talent that can line up beside Chambliss. Shekai Mills-Knight, when utilized by Baker, has been a revelation for Ole Miss' rushing attack; the only issue is that Knight has been used nowhere near enough. Makhi Frazier has left a lot to be desired since arriving at Ole Miss from Michigan State, and with Knight receiving the leftover touches, the Rebels have seen what the sophomore back is capable of. If Shekai Mills-Knight is given an uptick in touches in Norman, there is no reason that the tailback cannot eclipse Ole Miss' single-game leading rusher this season: Kewan Lacy's 122-yard showing against Missouri. The Rebels need to be more dynamic offensively, and it all starts with feeding the Canadian native. The Defense Holds Oklahoma Under 21 Georgia's offense was able to do whatever it wanted in Oxford last weekend, and the Rebels will need to suffocate John Mateer and the Sooners under the new Jason Witten-led offense. Ole Miss has lived off of its offense for the past two seasons, and with how things have gone recently, a strong defensive showing in Norman will go a long way, not just towards a win but towards proving to the selection committee that the Rebels are worthy of making the postseason. Golding's defense has the talent to be great, now it just needs to translate to the field. Running back Tory Blaylock had seen an uptick in carries in the last four games and even competed to lead the backfield since he was finally healthy again. Now, he's banged up again. Blaylock has rushed for 178 yards on 42 attempts in eight games this season. He had a season-high 12 carries for 71 yards against Mississippi State. He's still RB2 behind Lloyd Avant, but he should get more touches than usual in a game that interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten will have to rely on the ground attack in while rain pours down. His 513 receiving yards and four touchdowns have made him one of the Cardinals’ most productive offensive weapons. Louisville’s offense is set to receive a timely boost as the Cardinals prepare for their road matchup against North Carolina. Nakos also highlighted McCoy’s production this season. writing: “(McCoy) Has 25 catches for 513 yards and 4 TDs this season. Cardinals are at North Carolina.” McCoy last played against Syracuse on October 17. He caught five passes for 93 yards in Louisville’s 34-26 victory. Further testing revealed that the injury was more serious than initially believed. The wide receiver subsequently missed Louisville’s games against Stanford and Georgia Tech. Louisville head coach Jeff Brohm initially provided a cautious update about McCoy’s recovery ahead of the Stanford game on Oct. 31. Speaking about the injury, Brohm said : “I don’t think it requires surgery, but we have to get it healed. The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech . Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia . The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. The game was originally scheduled for the 7:30 p.m. ET primetime slot on Saturday, but due to travel issues caused by the FAA shutdown on Friday , kickoff was moved to 10:30 p.m. for this pivotal showdown. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier : The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The pass rush is going to be their best weapon to accomplish both of those goals, and if Arizona is going to pull off the upset, expect the pass rush to be leading the charge. Utah vs. Arizona prediction, picks The Wildcats are a good football team and should provide a big test for the Utes coming off last week's win. That said, so far this season, when Arizona has played the best teams in the Big 12, it has proven to be lagging just a bit behind. Over 60 minutes, I expect that to be the case again on Saturday, even with a raucous environment in Tucson for their biggest home game in years. Utah won't have it easy, but when the clock hits triple zeroes, I expect the Utes to move to 10-0 and cover the short number.
